Football Field
1.
Question: Given a football field in form of a Grid of size n x n and
each cell represents the skills of players in that particular cell.
We need to find an area (grid) of size k x k with the highest
average.
In short: Given a matrix of size n and a value k we had to find the
maximum possible sum of a submatrix of size k and then divide by
k*k to get the average.
Solution: This was basically 2D in Kadane Problem. You can refer
to this for the approach. Here there were some changes to be
made in the pre-written code. The function was given as one with
the int return type. But the average can be double as well with the
precision set to 2. This wasn't mentioned anywhere in the
question. You might be expected to interpret a few things from
the test cases provided. I was able to pass 8/11 test cases.
Community of Coders

2. Catch the Thief
Question: Given the values of skill and the bike’s power for the
thief. The performance of the thief was defined as the product of
skill and power. Similarly, we were given lists of skills and bike
power for the guards. We were expected to find the number of
combinations where the performance of every guard is greater
than that of the thief
In short: Find combinations that satisfy the given constraints.
Solution: I tried to form different combinations in cases where
they did not follow the constraints and subtracted them from the
possible number of combinations. I also optimised the solution
and was able to pass 6/12 test cases.

INTERVIEW FIRST ROUND
(AROUND 45MIN)
16/08/2022
For the first round, 36 people were short-listed. Our interviews
were conducted offline. We were asked to report at 8:30 am
sharp with 3 copies of resumes and College IDs. The actual
interview began around 9:45. We were divided into groups and
were sent accordingly.
 
        First, the Lady Interviewer greeted me with a smile. She
appreciated my resume a lot for about 2-3 minutes (about my
projects and my work). This made me feel very comfortable. 
She then asked me to Introduce myself - Always be prepared with
a short introduction of about 60 to 75 seconds. 
Flow that I followed for my intro: Name - Branch - CGPA -
Interests(Dev/DSAor 
Cp) 
- 
Participation 
(Teamwork 
and
hackathons ) - Current Work( working on a client project so and
so..) - Personal hobbies.
 Then she asked me about the client project which I mentioned
during the intro. You might expect a few questions from your
intro as well. I explained everything about the project.
Community of Coders

Flow that I followed for the explanation of a project: What (tech
stack n features) - why (use cases) - when (start time) - future
scope - team size
Make sure that you say only about what you have done. Be honest
during the interview. Interviewers are really very smart and tend
to ask counter-questions and explanations as well.
       In my resume, I had some projects developed using Flask. So
she asked me about flask and why I used Flask specifically. 
Flow that I followed for the explanation: About Flask - Uses -
Benefits - Advantages over Django  -  its use in my project
Be prepared for the questions on the frameworks, Languages,
and Tech Stack used in projects. You can prepare for this from
the interview bit.
         Also, I mentioned SQLite Database in my resume. She started
by asking about ACID properties (explanation and example). Then
asked me about the entire workflow of connecting the SQLite
database with my project and the code too for the queries and
connection (basically the methods involved). Also before the
interview just go through all your project on GitHub the code as
well as the explanation from the readme.
Community of Coders

As my expertise was app dev. She asked me what if they give me a web
project to work on. I answered this by prioritizing the learning aspect and
working more energetically. Always they expect you to be a good learner so
frame your replies to give them such an impression.
            Then she asked me to imagine a situation where I was arranging a party.
And I give tickets containing ordered numbers to each person (1..2..3..so on).
Now at the end, I randomly pick a number and declare the winner as the person
with a ticket containing the same number. Here she wanted to know about the
different data structures I can think of. I asked her questions like what I need to
store and what the expected output is.. Do I need a generator function …. Always
asks questions and get your doubts cleared before you start discussing the
solution. Then I started with arrays, linked lists and maps (explanation and time
complexity). 
                 She then asked me a coding question :
Question: Given an array of 0s and 1s. I need to cluster the 1s at specific
locations such that I do a minimum no of swaps. (of 0s and 1s)
Eg Array [ 0, 1, 0 , 0 , 1 , 0 , 1]
Here we hav 3 ones which can v=be clustered as  [ 1 , 1, 1 , 0 , 0 , 0 , 0] (2 swaps) 
 [ 0, 1 , 1 , 1 , 0 , 0 ,0] (2 swaps)
 [ 0, 0, 1 , 1 , 1 , 0 , 0] (2 swaps)
[ 0, 0, 0 , 1 , 1 , 1 , 0] (2 swaps)
[ 0, 0, 0 , 0 , 1 , 1, 1] (1 swap)
So the 1s can be clustered anywhere we just need to minimise the swaps. 
Community of Coders

Solution: 
First I started with the approach of the pointer. Always discuss your
solutions with the interviewer.
Then while explaining the same I understood that it was a sliding window
problem.
Here the sum of the array would give the number of 1s and this would act as the
length of the window. Check the sum of the first window ⇒ number of 1s in that
window.
Then the number of zeros would be nothing but the number of swaps for
clustering the 1s in that window.
Array [ 0, 1, 0 , 0 , 1 , 0 , 1]
Sum  = 3 (no of 1s)
Window size = sum = 3
First window Array [ 0, 1, 0 , 0 , 1 , 0 , 1] ⇒ sum_of win = 1 
So the number of swaps for this window ⇒ Sum - sum_of_win = 3 -1 =2
For the next window just check the incoming and outgoing values. 
Array [ 0, 1, 0 , 0 , 1 , 0 , 1] 
If same the no changes in sum_of win
Else if incoming is 1 and outgoing is 0 ⇒ sum_of win++
Else if incoming is 0 and outgoing is 1 ⇒ sum_of win- -
Then store the min Value for each iteration as mn = min (mn, Sum - sum_of_win )
          She asked me to write the pseudo-code. Always keep a habit of explaining
the code while writing. Explaining each module, time complexity and also dry run
on one of the test cases.
              Then at the end, she asked if I had any questions for her. I asked her to
suggest changes in my resume this helped me to understand how an
interviewer goes through your resume.
Community of Coders

ROUND (AROUND 1HR)

Find the starting character of string 1 in string 2 
Say you found it at loc (int)
If not found then return false
Then iterate through each character starting the string 1
from 0 and string2 from the loc.
After some time we were sent for the second round of
interviews. I was asked purely DSA questions this round.
First, the interviewer asked me to introduce myself. 
Then 
DSA Question 1 :
Given a 2D matrix of 0s and 1s where 1s repent paths and 0s
represent blocks. I was asked to find the longest possible path
between source and destination. I was also provided with
coordinates for the same.
Solution: I had practised this variety on Leetcode.  Using
DFS+backtracking I was able to solve this question. I was asked to
write the entire code.  Explain the modules, and the flow, dry run
it on one of the test cases and discuss the time complexity.
DSA Question 2 :
Given two strings check if one was formed by rotating the other.
Solution: Always start with a brute-force approach.
Approach 1:  
Community of Coders

Check for equality of each value if not equal at any point
return false
Return true at the end of the iteration.
Append the string2 with itself and find the string1 in the
resultant string.
If found return true
Else return false
Here this can be solved using hashing such that given a node
as key to the hashmap it would return the parent of that node
(immediate ancestor).
Use BFS to populate the hashmap
For the root node, it would give null as a parent.
After this over a while loop checks if node1 exists in the
ancestry of node2 if yes then return true 
Else check again over a while loop check if node2 exists in the
ancestry of node1 if yes then return true 
Else return false
Approach 2:  
Eg string1 = “tree” , string2 =”etre”
New_string = string2 +string2 ⇒ “etreetre”
DSA Question 3:
Given a tree (not a BST) check if the given path is valid.
Here I was given two nodes and I was expected to check if one
was the child of the other. Also, the nodes would be given in any
order ie 
Parent, child ⇒ true
Child, parent ⇒ true
Child, child ⇒ false

He said he was satisfied with all the answers.
He finally asked if I had any questions for him. I asked what the
interns do at GS. He explained the project and presentation in
about 3-4mins. I again asked for a review of my resume.
Also, do ask questions bcoz this shows ur interest in that
particular company.
Some of us got selected after 2 rounds of interviews(including
me) and some after 3. So you never know if you are selected or
not until the results are declared at the end. After my second
round, I wasn't called for the third round and was disappointed
but still was confident about my performance during the
interview.
